text:
james: Kicking off a canary for the new routing policy (policy-v3) -> 15% traffic at 13:07 PT. Console: https://console.redwood.ai/rollouts/456

deploy-bot: CANARY_STARTED policy-v3 -> 15% traffic (canary id: canary-456) by james at 13:07

marta: Saw a spike in 5xxs and tail latency right after the first batch. sample log: `ERR: route_lookup: key-mismatch` and `latency_p95: 420ms -> 980ms`

ryan: Can we do a fast revert? If we set the traffic split back to 0% and flip to policy-v2 it should be instant. Need to think about caches/KV though.

james: Agreed on fast revert. Question: will rolling back create stale KV entries? We have prefix caching for route meta. Do we need to purge anything?

marta: Short answer: yes, potential for stale prefix cache. Longer: canary writes go to same KV namespaces but with a canary prefix `c456:`. If we just shift traffic away, the stable path should be fine. But if code changes touched schema, stale entries could cause odd lookups when traffic returns.

sre-oncall: Plan suggestion: (1) set canary split -> 0% (2) enable circuit-breaker on policy-v3 to prevent accidental routes (3) run prefix invalidation for `c456-` in KV service (non-blocking) (4) monitor errors/latency for 10m.

marta: For (3) we have a safe invalidation command. Use admin API:
```
POST /admin/cache/invalidate_prefix
{
  "namespace": "routes-kv",
  "prefix": "c456-"
}
```
This marks keys and asynchronously clears cached prefixes. Do NOT do a full namespace purge unless you want widespread cache misses.

ryan: If anyone's worried about race windows, we can also set a guard flag in the routing metadata so policy-v3 returns 503 for any requests while toggled. That stops any spillover until KV is quiet.

james: ok i'm going to apply traffic change now. Doing: `PATCH /rollouts/456` with payload to set splits.

marta: payload example (for the console API):
```
PATCH /api/rollout/456
{
  "splits": [
    {"policy": "policy-v2", "weight": 100},
    {"policy": "policy-v3", "weight": 0}
  ],
  "guard": {"circuit_breaker": {"enabled": true}}
}
```

deploy-bot: ROLLOUT_UPDATED canary-456 -> splits applied (v2:100%, v3:0%) by james at 13:09

james: Triggering KV prefix invalidation now.

deploy-bot: KV_INVALIDATION_QUEUED prefix=c456- request_id=inv-8921 by james

marta: I also ran a targeted read-check to make sure stable keys are intact: `GET /kv/routes-kv/canonical-route-42` returned expected v2 entry. No schema drift observed.

ryan: Telemetry note: we need the per-split error rates in the console while rollback is happening. devex-bot can we spin up a temporary dashboard showing split-by-error/p95/token-cost?

devex-bot: Created temp dashboard: Rollout-456-rollback (panels: split-error-rate, split-p95, per-route-tokens). Link: https://console.redwood.ai/dash/rollback-456

sre-oncall: Invalidation completed: inv-8921 status=done (took ~18s). Circuit-breaker on policy-v3 is active. Monitoring 10m window.

marta: Quick checklist we followed: 1) flip traffic to stable 2) enable guard 3) queue prefix invalidation 4) verify reads against stable 5) watch telemetry. Good pattern for future fast-reverts.

james: Rollback looks clean. p95 back to baseline, no new 5xx. I'm removing canary resources (scale to 0) and leaving the guard for another 5m.

ryan: Follow-ups: (A) add a CLI shortcut `redwood rollback fast --canary-id` that does split flip + prefix invalidation + guard toggle, (B) tweak rollout UX to show cache-invalidations as an atomic step in the console.

marta: Also add a warning in the rollout docs about shared KV namespaces vs per-canary prefixes. We should recommend one of: per-canary prefix OR schema-stable migrations only.

james: thumbs up :thumbsup: Rollback complete at 13:16. I'll open a short postmortem doc with timeline and the commands used.

sre-oncall: Logged incident note: INC-2026-03-18-01, severity=low, root cause = routing policy v3 introduced unexpected key lookup pattern.

marta: TODO for engineering: automate the prefix invalidator so it becomes part of the rollback playbook (ticket created: ENGPLAT-789).

james: Thanks all. Good catch on telemetry and guarding.
